occasions.name: Vinayaka Chaturthi (Ganesh Chaturthi)
occasions.description: Celebration of the manifestation of Lord Ganesha, remover of all obstacles and Lord of beginnings.
occasions.significance: Celebrated on Shukla Paksha Chaturthi of Bhadrapada month. Devotees install clay idols, perform pranapratishta, offer modakas and durva grass, and chant Vedic stotras.
occasions.whatHappensToday: Homes and public pandals are vibrantly adorned. Prana Pratishtha rituals invoke Ganesha into sacred clay murtis with Vedic mantras. Shodashopachara puja is offered featuring 21 modakas, red hibiscus flowers, and durva grass blades.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Bathe at dawn and wear clean clothes (yellow or red).
2. Prepare or place clay Ganesha on a wooden altar facing east or north.
3. Light an oil/ghee lamp and offer incense.
4. Recite Sri Mahaganapathi Dhyanam and Sri Sankata Nashana Ganesha Stotram.
5. Offer 21 durva grass blades and modakas with sincere devotion.
6. Conclude with Maha Ganesha Pancharatnam and seek blessings for wisdom.

occasions.name: Sri Mahaganapathi Homam – Chennai Campus
occasions.description: Official institutional Ganapathi Homam at Amrita School of Engineering, Chennai, for faculty, staff, and students.
occasions.significance: Conducted under the divine auspices and guidance of Mata Amritanandamayi Devi (Amma) for academic excellence, inner harmony, and removal of impediments.
occasions.whatHappensToday: Department of Amrita Darshanam conducts the sacred Ganapathi Homa in the central campus quadrangle. Special parayanam chants accompany the fire offerings, concluded by prasadam distribution.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Assemble at the campus yajnashala by 6:30 AM.
2. Participate in Sri Amma Dhyanam opening contemplation.
3. Join the collective recitation of Sri Mahaganapathi Dhyanam, Sankata Nashana Stotram, and Ganesha Pancharatnam.
4. Offer sacred samit sticks into the homa fire at Poornahuti.
5. Receive sanctified prasadam and take a vow for academic discipline.

occasions.name: Maha Shivaratri (The Great Night of Shiva)
occasions.description: The sacred night celebrating the cosmic dance of Lord Shiva (Tandava) and the emergence of the Jyotirlinga.
occasions.significance: Celebrated on Magha Krishna Chaturdashi. A night of intense wakefulness (Jagaran), fasting, and four-prahara abhishekam symbolizing transcendence of the mind.
occasions.whatHappensToday: Temples reverberate with Panchakshari japa (Om Namah Shivaya). Devotees observe strict fasting (Nirahara or Phalahara). Continuous Abhishekam of the Shiva Lingam with milk, curd, honey, ghee, sugar, and holy ash takes place throughout the four quarters of the night.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Begin with early morning Snana and Sankalpa for Shivaratri vrata.
2. Observe fasting throughout the day and night.
3. Chant Sri Shiva Panchakshari Stotram, Lingashtakam, and Bilvashtakam during the four Praharas.
4. Offer fresh Bilva leaves on the Shiva Lingam.
5. Maintain quietude and meditation; break the fast at dawn the following morning.

occasions.name: Nirjala Ekadashi (Bhima Ekadashi)
occasions.description: The most sacred and austere of all 24 Ekadashis, observed without even drinking water for immense spiritual purification.
occasions.significance: Falling in Jyeshtha Shukla Paksha, it is said that observing Nirjala Ekadashi grants the combined spiritual merit of observing all twenty-four Ekadashis of the year.
occasions.whatHappensToday: Devotees observe a complete fast from sunrise on Ekadashi until sunrise on Dwadashi without water. Vishnu Sahasranama parayanam and night vigil are performed.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Fast from water and food from sunrise to sunrise.
2. Meditate on Lord Vishnu's lotus feet.
3. Recite Sri Vishnu Sahasranamam and Achyutashtakam.
4. Break the fast on Dwadashi morning after offering water and food to the needy.

occasions.name: Vaikuntha Ekadashi & Gita Jayanti
occasions.description: Celebration of the opening of the heavenly gates of Vaikuntha and the sacred anniversary of the revelation of Srimad Bhagavad Gita.
occasions.significance: Occurring on Margashirsha Shukla Ekadashi. Devotees pass through the Vaikuntha Dwaram (Gate of Heaven) in temples and recite the entire Bhagavad Gita and Vishnu Sahasranamam.
occasions.whatHappensToday: Massive pre-dawn gatherings in Vishnu temples (such as Srirangam, Tirumala, and Guruvayur). The Paramapada Vasal opens with ecstatic chanting. Complete chapters of the Gita and thousand names of Vishnu are recited.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Wake up during Brahma Muhurta and take a sacred bath.
2. Observe Ekadashi fast (abstain from grains and beans).
3. Recite Sri Vishnu Sahasranamam and Achyutashtakam.
4. Read and reflect upon key verses of the Bhagavad Gita.

occasions.name: Pradosha Vratam (Sacred Twilight of Lord Shiva)
occasions.description: Fortnightly observance on Trayodashi Tithi (13th lunar day) dedicated to Lord Shiva during the holy sunset twilight (Sandhya Kala).
occasions.significance: During Pradosha twilight, Lord Shiva dances with Goddess Parvati on Mount Kailash to remove the karmic bondage of sincere seekers.
occasions.whatHappensToday: Devotees fast through the afternoon. Between 4:30 PM and 6:30 PM, Shiva Lingam and Nandi are bathed in Panchamrita, offered bilva leaves, and worshipped with fragrant lamps.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Fast during the day until the Pradosha puja concludes.
2. Light an oil lamp at home or temple during twilight.
3. Chant Sri Shiva Panchakshari Stotram, Lingashtakam, and Bilvashtakam.
4. Circumambulate the Nandi and Shiva Lingam.
5. Break fast with simple satvik prasadam.

occasions.name: Sankashti Chaturthi (Sankatahara Chaturthi)
occasions.description: Monthly fast on Krishna Paksha Chaturthi dedicated to Lord Ganesha for swift deliverance from all worldly crises and debts.
occasions.significance: Mentioned in the Bhavishya and Narasimha Puranas. Observed from dawn till the sighting of the moon at night.
occasions.whatHappensToday: Devotees fast through the day, recite Sankata Nashana Stotram, and at moonrise perform Arghya to the Moon and Ganesha before breaking the fast.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Observe strict fasting during daytime.
2. Recite Sri Sankata Nashana Ganesha Stotram thrice during the day.
3. At moonrise, offer clean water, flowers, and sandalwood paste toward the moon.
4. Offer sweet modakas to Ganesha and break fast with prasad.

occasions.name: Vasant Panchami (Saraswati Puja)
occasions.description: Celebration of the advent of spring and the manifestation of Goddess Saraswati, patron of intellect, learning, music, and wisdom.
occasions.significance: Observed on Magha Shukla Panchami. Sacred day for Aksharabhyasa (initiation of children into the alphabet and education).
occasions.whatHappensToday: Books, pens, and musical instruments are placed before the altar. Students and teachers wear yellow attire, offer yellow flowers, and chant Saraswati Stotram.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Bathe early and wear yellow garments.
2. Place books, notebooks, and writing instruments on the altar.
3. Offer yellow flowers and sweet saffron rice (kesar bhat).
4. Chant Sri Saraswati Stotram (Ya Kundendu Tushara) and seek blessings for sharp memory and intuition.

occasions.name: Deepavali (Diwali Lakshmi Puja)
occasions.description: The festival of lights symbolizing the victory of spiritual light over darkness, truth over ignorance, and divine wealth over despair.
occasions.significance: Celebrated on Kartika Amavasya. Homes and business establishments are cleansed and adorned with glowing earthen oil lamps (diyas).
occasions.whatHappensToday: Pre-dawn oil bath (Ganga Snana), wearing new garments, exchanging sweets, drawing colorful rangoli kolams, lighting terracotta diyas, and performing the evening Mahalakshmi and Ganesha Puja.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Take a traditional oil bath in the early morning.
2. Cleanse the prayer room and decorate the threshold with diyas.
3. In the evening (Pradosha Muhurta), seat idols of Lakshmi and Ganesha together.
4. Recite Sri Mahalakshmi Ashtakam and Sri Maha Ganesha Pancharatnam.
5. Offer lotus flowers, kheer, and coin offerings for auspicious abundance.

occasions.name: Guru Purnima (Sri Vyasa Puja)
occasions.description: The full moon day dedicated to honoring the spiritual master, lineage of teachers, and Sage Veda Vyasa.
occasions.significance: Falling on Ashadha Purnima. Monastics begin their Chaturmasya vrata; students express gratitude to preceptors and spiritual guides.
occasions.whatHappensToday: Devotees worship the sacred Guru Padukas (sandals). Discourses on spiritual lineage and meditation sessions take place in ashrams and educational institutions.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Meditate on the spiritual preceptor during early morning.
2. Chant Sri Guru Stotram (Gurur Brahma).
3. Express heartfelt reverence and gratitude to teachers, parents, and guides.
4. Offer flowers, fruits, and dakshina to spiritual institutions.

occasions.name: Sri Hanuman Jayanti
occasions.description: Celebration of the birth of Lord Hanuman, the quintessential devotee, embodiment of strength, wisdom, and humility.
occasions.significance: Celebrated on Chaitra Purnima (in North and Western India) and Margashirsha (in South India). Known for continuous recitation of Hanuman Chalisa.
occasions.whatHappensToday: Hanuman shrines are anointed with vermilion paste (sindoor) and mustard oil. Devotees offer sweet boondi, laddoos, and betel leaf garlands while reciting Hanuman Chalisa 108 times.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Cleanse the altar and light a ghee lamp.
2. Apply orange sindoor to Lord Hanuman's lotus feet.
3. Recite Sri Hanuman Chalisa with deep devotion.
4. Distribute prasadam to birds, animals, or children in honor of the Lord.

occasions.name: Ratha Saptami (Surya Jayanti)
occasions.description: Celebration of the Sun God turning His chariot toward the northern hemisphere (Uttarayana).
occasions.significance: Falling on Magha Shukla Saptami. Dedicated to health, vitality, eye sight, and dispelling dark mental fatigue.
occasions.whatHappensToday: Devotees take an auspicious bath placing seven Calotropis (Erukkam / Arka) leaves on the head, shoulders, and knees. Milk is boiled in earthen pots under direct sunlight until it overflows.
occasions.preparationGuide:
1. Take a sacred morning bath facing the rising sun.
2. Offer Arghya (water, red flowers, and rice) to Lord Surya.
3. Recite Sri Aditya Hridaya Stotram.
4. Cook sweet rice in sunlight and offer it to the Sun God.
